previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of atrial fibrillation, systolic heart failure (EF 30%), diabetes, obesity, and recent stroke was admitted for intermittent left-sided chest pain that began the morning of admission. The pain was dull, associated with nausea, worsened by movement and lying down, and partially attributed to muscle strain after heavy lifting and possible GERD from a spicy meal. Initial evaluation showed no acute myocardial infarction on EKG, but troponins trended slightly upward before declining, suggesting demand ischemia. Elevated BNP and chest X-ray findings indicated acute on chronic heart failure exacerbation due to volume overload, likely from dietary indiscretion. He was treated with intravenous and oral diuretics, resulting in significant fluid loss and symptom improvement. Hypokalemia triggered episodes of ventricular tachycardia, which resolved with potassium repletion. His atrial fibrillation remained rate-controlled, and INR was therapeutic. Chest pain resolved with morphine and supportive care. Medications were adjusted at discharge, including increased metoprolol and aspirin, short-term increased Lasix, and potassium supplementation. A sleep clinic follow-up was arranged to address obstructive sleep apnea and pulmonary hypertension.

Brief Hospital Course:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: ___ y/o w/ HTN, HLD, sCHF EF 30%, afib, DM2, 
morbid obesity, who presents with burning sensation ___ chest and 
shortness of breath.  
.  
#) Chest burning sensation - He remained asymptomatic since 
presentation.  Troponins were baseline at .03 and EKG showed no 
ST-T changes, ACS was ruled out.  Character of pain was burning 
and nonexertional, not reproducible on exam, so likely GERD ___ 
setting of alcohol consumption, or musculoskeletal.  
.
#) Acute on chronic systolic CHF exacerbation - He has a hx sCHF 
and evidence of hypervolemia on admission exam ___ edema, JVD, 
hepatomegaly). Initial exacerbating factor was likely dietary, 
endorses eating soup which he typically does not. We kept him on 
80 IV Lasix BID with goal 2L negative per day initially, then 
switched to torsemide 60mg PO BID for increased diuresis as he 
was not meeting goal. This regimen worked well and he was 
diuresed from an admission weight of 348 lb to 330lbs on 
discharge. His dry weight is unclear but is likely somewhere 
around 325-330lbs. His SOB and b/l ___ edema improved remarkably. 
He was discharged on torsemide 40mg daily instead of lasix, as 
he had had a good response to it.  Because of some hypotension 
during this admission, his spironolactone was held for the time 
being, and can be restarted ___ the outpatient setting as blood 
pressures allow.  
.
#) Foot cellulitis - During admission, developed right foot 
cellulitis and a fluid pocket. Wound I&D'ed by surgery and 
podiatry x 2 at bedside with no need for OR at this time.  
Podiatry contacted and had low suspicion for osteomyelitis, and 
did not want to do further debridements and did not recommend 
getting an MRI, recommended outpatient followup. Cultures grew 
MSSA. He was on vancomycin for 1 week, and per ID consultation 
will get an additional 2 weeks fo dicloxacillin. He will have 
podiatry f/u ___ the outpatient setting. 
.
#) Afib and Anticoagulation - Subtherapeutic INR at presentation 
was 1.5 and has had poor INR control chronically. CHADS score of 
5 with previous stroke, had discussion of initiating pradaxa 
given fluctuating INRs. Transitioned to Pradaxa during 
admission.  
.
#) Change ___ bowel movements - Reported maroon stools, but 
rectal exam showed brown stools, guaic negative and no gross 
blood.  Suspicion for GI bleed was low, no black stool or BRBPR 
on hx, Hct was stable.         
.  
#) DM2 - Poorly controlled, recent A1c was 9.4%. He was kept on 
an insulin sliding scale and NPH BID. He currently is on NPH 
BID, but was intermittently mildly hypoglycemic so his home 
dosing was decreased. He will follow-up with ___. As 
he normally only takes NPH once daily at home (compliance 
issues), he may benefit from glargine instead. 
.
#) HTN/HLD: continued metoprolol, ramipril, and pravastatin 
continued. Spironolactone held ___ issues with hypotension that 
may have been more related to foot infection than drug effect; 
can consider restarting spironolactone ___ outpatient setting.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Recurrent chest pain, shortness of breath, CHF exacerbation with
asymmetric lower extremities; assess for right lower extremity DVT.

COMPARISONS:  None available.

FINDINGS:  Grayscale and color Doppler sonography was performed of the right
lower extremity.  Normal compressibility and flow was seen in the right common
femoral, superficial femoral, popliteal, peroneal, and posterior tibial veins
without evidence of DVT.

IMPRESSION:  No right lower extremity DVT.

CT RIGHT LWOER EXTREMITY WITH CONTRAST, ___.

CLINICAL INDICATION:   ___ man with CHF exacerbation, right foot
cellulitis on antibiotics.  New fever and pain shooting up right foot.  Assess
for necrotizing fasciitis or any clear signs of infection in the right lower
extremity.

COMPARISON:  None available.

TECHNIQUE:  Right lower extremity CT after the uneventful intravenous
administration of 100 mL Omnipaque contrast material with multiple contiguous
axial MDCT images on soft tissue and bone algorithms through the right foot
and ankle with coronal and sagittal reformations provided for interpretation.

FINDINGS:

There is a mild amount of subcutaneous soft tissue edema and skin thickening
at the anterolateral dorsum of foot posteriorly and in the right ankle,
cutaneous and subcutaneous soft tissues, incompletely seen.  There are no soft
tissue foci of gas or rim-enhancing fluid collections identified.  No definite
osseous erosions or periostitis or skin defects extending to bone.

Mild tarsometatarsal degenerative changes are seen, most prevalent at the
third tarsometatarsal joint, with subjacent subchondral cystic changes. 
Subchondral cystic changes are noted also at the cuboid articulation with the
fourth and fifth metatarsals.

There is a regular ossific density projecting at the level of the tibiofibular
syndesmosis, incompletely seen, and likely reflecting the sequela of prior
trauma or injury.  Incidental note is made of a prominent os trigonum, type 2
os naviculare and bipartite medial sesamoid.

The plantar fascia, medial flexor tendons, peroneus brevis and longus and
anterior tibialis and extensor tendons appear grossly maintained on soft
tissue windows.  There is mild thickening of the Achilles tendon (3:28),
approximately 4 cm proximal to distal attachment upon the posterior calcaneus.

There is calcified atherosclerotic vascular disease involving the posterior
tibial artery and dorsalis pedis. The arterial vasculature appears patent
otherwise with contrast material extending into the posterior tibial artery
and dorsalis pedis artery.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No CT evidence of osteomyelitis, soft tissue abscess or radiographic signs
of necrotizing fasciitis.

2.  Mild cutaneous and subcutaneous soft tissue edema and thickening involving
the anterolateral dorsum of foot and ankle consistent with cellulitis and/or
nonspecific edema in the appropriate clinical setting.

3.  Irregular ossific density at the tibiofibular syndesmosis, likely
reflecting sequela of prior remote injury.

4.  Mild degenerative changes at the tarsometatarsal joints, predominantly at
the third tarsometatarsal joint.

5.  Calcified atherosclerotic vascular disease involving the posterior tibial
artery and dorsalis pedis, which are otherwise patent.

6.  Achilles tendinopathy, approximately 4 cm proximal to distal calcaneal
attachment.

Important findings were discussed directly with Dr. ___ at
approximately 10:55 a.m. on ___ by musculoskeletal radiology fellow,
Dr. ___, via phone.

INDICATION:  CHF exacerbation, right foot cellulitis, on antibiotics, new
fever and cough; question of pneumonia.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph on ___.

FINDINGS:  PA and lateral views of the chest.  Better lung volumes compared to
most recent study.  Moderate cardiomegaly is stable.  Unchanged mild pulmonary
vascular congestion, no pulmonary edema.  The mediastinal and hilar contours
and pleural surfaces are normal.  Mild linear atelectasis in the left mid
lung.  

IMPRESSION:
1.  No evidence of pneumonia.
2.  Unchanged mild pulmonary vascular congestion.  No pulmonary edema.
